newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish customs officers stage go-slow over pay.
newsitem.headline: Polish customs officers stage go-slow over pay.

text.p: Employees of Poland's customs office on Sunday staged a four-hour go-slow to back demands for a new pay agreement, private Radio Zet reported.
The customs officers caused queues at the borders by carrying out unusually meticulous checks of travellers, documents and goods in what is known in Poland as an "Italian strike".
The radio said the go-slow, staged after pay negotiations collapsed on Saturday, was carried out more extensively along Poland's western border with Germany than along the eastern frontier.
The protesters are demanding bonuses no lower than 100 percent of their basic pay plus benefits, PAP news agency reported Ewa Dabrowska of the customs' employees' trade union as saying.
Andrzej Gajda, a union spokesman, said Sunday's protest would be followed by an all-day action on Monday.
The go-slow involves scrupulously checking a full one-half of the traffic crossing Poland's borders rather than the customary 10 percent, Gajda explained.
